title: Keep Message StateChange for uncarried changes
description:
Oracle: jmap-chat-spec 6bcd9d8 (quoted text). Mapped by wf_6712c4f8-c2b.

[chat-ext] ChatMessagePush must not suppress Message StateChange for uncarried changes
Spec (db880a1): draft-atwood-jmap-chat-push-00.md L108: "A `ChatMessagePush` stands in for the `StateChange` that the arrival of the messages it carries would otherwise cause. Every other change in the account is still announced by a standard `StateChange`, as {{RFC8620}} Section 7 describes: this includes Message changes that the payload does not carry (edits, destroys, the owner's own messages, and messages excluded by `ChatPushConfig`, mute, or block) and changes to every other data type."
Code: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/push.rs:151-191 chat_state_change_for removes "Message" for every account with a live chatPush entry; crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/chat_push_validation.rs:191,222 (oracle quotes the old text)
Now: With chatPush set, the Message type is dropped from every StateChange for that account. A client therefore never hears about edits, destroys, its own messages from other devices, or messages filtered by config, mute, or block.
Change: Drop Message from the StateChange only when every Message change in the batch was carried by a delivered ChatMessagePush. For example, the caller passes, per account, whether uncarried Message changes exist, and Message is kept when they do. Re-cite L108 in the docs and tests.
